From Enumclaw, drive SR-410 east to the White River entrance of Mount Rainier National Park, turn right onto Sunrise Road and go about 5 miles, cross the White River, then turn left onto White River Road and follow it to its end at the campground. White River Road closes for the winter.
The road to Mowich Lake is closed to vehicles at the Fairfax Bridge on SR-165, which is closed to cars, bicycles and pedestrians; there is no alternate route and the park lists no other way in.

From the Nisqually entrance of Mount Rainier National Park (SR 706), drive east on the Nisqually-Longmire Road for 1 mile and turn left onto Westside Road. Follow it 3.2 miles to the closed gate at Dry Creek and park short of the barricade.

siblingApproaches.approach: From Paradise (5,400 ft), follow the Skyline Trail about a mile to Glacier Vista (about 6,300 ft), the usual rope-up point, and descend onto the Nisqually Glacier. Cross it and climb the gully on its far (west) side onto Wapowety Cleaver, then follow the cleaver crest to high camps, with old rock wind walls, at the edge of the Wilson Glacier, around 9,000–9,500 ft. From camp, cross the Wilson Glacier to the base of the Fuhrer Finger.

From White River Campground (4,400 ft) on SR 410, the Glacier Basin Trail climbs 3.5 miles through forest along the Inter Fork of the White River — several creek crossings and old avalanche/slide paths cross the trail — to Glacier Basin Campground (5,935 ft), which has six designated sites, a camp toilet, and a bear-proof food cache; this is the last reliable water source and the last forested camp. It's a well-built but relentlessly steep trail that gains the ridge via dozens of switchbacks, crossing a small cascading creek/waterfall repeatedly in the first mile through old-growth fir and hemlock (look for ~100-year-old fire-scarred cedar snags). siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: Start at the Rachel Lake Trailhead (Trail #1313, elev. ~2,800 ft) at the end of Box Canyon Road/FR-4930.

siblingApproaches.approach: Start at the Rachel Lake Trailhead (Trail #1313, elev. ~2,800 ft) at the end of Box Canyon Road/FR-4930. Follow the Rachel Lake Trail as it climbs gently through forest along the Box Canyon Creek drainage — the grade is easy and well-graded here, mostly Class 1 hiking. At roughly 2–2.2 miles and about 450–500 ft of gain (~3,300 ft elevation), the trail crosses a brushy avalanche-path clearing where Hibox's summit block comes into view on the ridge to the northeast; this clearing is the key landmark.
